notes: Test prompts for the skill. Each should end with a copy-paste brief in a single fenced block, a saved file, and a note telling the user to review the generated plan before approving it. Assertions are deliberately about brief STRUCTURE, not subject matter — the skill must work on any topic.

evals.name: engineering-comparison-casual
evals.prompt: ok so we're on elasticsearch for search, about 40M docs, and honestly the ops burden is killing us. someone on the team keeps pushing typesense. before I let this become a whole quarter of work I want gemini to actually dig into real benchmarks and not just vendor marketing pages. can you write me something I can paste in?
evals.expected_output: A scoping round (or stated defaults), then a copy-paste brief with: one-sentence objective naming the decision; explicit out-of-scope list; a source bar that names vendor marketing as disallowed or requires it be labelled vendor-run; named ordered output sections including a comparison table and a 'could not verify' section; a rule against comparing benchmark numbers measured under different conditions; DOI/URL citation requirement with a no-fabrication clause. Saved to a file. Handover note says to review the generated plan before approving.
assertions: Output contains exactly one fenced code block holding the complete brief
Brief states the objective in a single sentence and names the decision it serves
Brief contains an explicit out-of-scope or exclusions list
Brief's source-quality section names disallowed source types, not only preferred ones
Brief names output sections in an explicit order
Brief includes a section for what could not be verified
Brief forbids inventing citations/DOIs and requires DOI or direct URL
The brief is saved to a file and the path is reported
Handover instructs the user to review/edit the generated research plan before approving

evals.name: verification-of-secondhand-numbers
evals.prompt: I've got three thresholds in my draft that I pulled from a blog post and my advisor is going to ask where they came from. I need the primary sources, not another summary. Can you make me a gemini deep research prompt that verifies them properly?
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as the narrow-verification shape. Asks for the three figures verbatim (with units) if not supplied. Brief defines what counts as confirmation (issuing body's own document; a third-party quote does not count), makes 'not found' an acceptable well-specified outcome, and asks for a status table with document/section/URL per figure. Should not balloon into a literature survey.
assertions: Skill asks for the exact figures with units, or uses figures supplied by the user verbatim
Brief states that a number quoted by a third party does not count as confirmation
Brief makes 'not found' an explicitly acceptable outcome rather than requiring an answer
Brief requests document title, section/page and direct URL per verified figure
Brief stays scoped to verification and does not request a broad literature survey
Output contains exactly one fenced code block holding the complete brief

evals.name: thai-request-market-landscape
evals.prompt: ทำ prompt ให้ gemini deep research หน่อย เรื่อง carbon credit registry standards ที่ใช้กันในเอเชีย ต้องเอาไปเสนอทีมสัปดาห์หน้า อยากได้ตารางเทียบด้วย
evals.expected_output: Responds in Thai. Treats it as a landscape-survey shape narrowing to a comparison. Brief includes geography scope (Asia) with explicit exclusions, a comparison table with named columns, source bar preferring registry/standards-body primary documents over vendor material, and a 'sources disagree' section. Notes the audience is the user's team and the decision it supports.
assertions: Reply to the user is in Thai
Brief includes an explicit geographic scope and exclusions
Brief requests a comparison table with named columns
Brief prefers primary standards-body or registry documents over vendor/marketing material
Brief includes a section surfacing disagreement between sources
Output contains exactly one fenced code block holding the complete brief
